facets.core_claim: Centeotl is the maize itself; from his body came the food plants, and he is born anew each season.

facets.facet_name: The Dual Lord-and-Lady in the thirteenth heaven
facets.core_claim: Ometeotl, mother and father of the gods, invented itself and from its duality engendered the four creator sons.

facets.facet_name: The Fifth Sun who demands blood to move
facets.core_claim: Tonatiuh rules the present age, Nahui Ollin; he will move only as long as he is fed with the hearts and blood of sacrifice.

facets.facet_name: The humble god who became the sun
facets.core_claim: Nanahuatzin offered only his scabs and his courage; he leapt into the fire and became Tonatiuh, while the rich Tecciztecatl, following, became the moon.

facets.facet_name: The proud god who became the moon
facets.core_claim: Tecciztecatl offered precious feathers and jade, but his courage failed; he followed into the fire and became the moon.

facets.facet_name: Precious Flower, goddess of love and beauty
facets.core_claim: Xochiquetzal brings desire, beauty and the flowering of life; artisans and lovers honor her with flowers.

facets.facet_name: Old Coyote, trickster of song and dance
facets.core_claim: Huehuecoyotl plays tricks on gods and humans alike, starts quarrels and parties, and sings and dances through the world.

facets.facet_name: The devouring earth from whose body the world was made
facets.core_claim: Tlaltecuhtli was ripped apart to make the earth; she gives all food from her body and hungers for hearts and blood in return.

facets.facet_name: Queen of the land of the dead
facets.core_claim: Mictecacihuatl guards the bones in the ninth level of Mictlan with her husband and presides over the feasts of the dead.

facets.facet_name: Dog who guides the dead and the setting sun
facets.core_claim: Xolotl leads the sun into the underworld each night and guides souls across the river of Mictlan; dogs buried with the dead are his.

facets.facet_name: Old God of the central fire
facets.core_claim: Xiuhtecuhtli is the fire at the navel of the world and of every home; when the cycle of 52 years ends, the new fire must be lit or the sun will not rise.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the maguey and pulque
facets.core_claim: Mayahuel's body became the maguey; its sap is her milk, the pulque that nourishes and intoxicates.

facets.facet_name: Death god, the bony one
facets.core_claim: The death god (God A) wears bells and skeletal bones; he rules Mitnal and comes to seize the dying.
facets.scholarly_note: The name "Ah Puch" is a later popular label; Classic inscriptions name death gods such as Kimi and the codices God A.

facets.facet_name: The one god without image
facets.core_claim: Hunab Ku is the only true god, without body or image, from whom all the other gods descend.
facets.scholarly_note: Known only from colonial-era Yucatec sources compiled under missionary influence; many scholars read Hunab Ku as a colonial construction shaped by Christian monotheism rather than a pre-Hispanic deity.

facets.facet_name: Sovereign Framer who creates by the word
facets.core_claim: Tepeu and Gucumatz sat in the water wrapped in light; they spoke, and said "Earth," and the earth arose.

facets.facet_name: Plumed Serpent who creates through speech
facets.core_claim: Gucumatz, covered in blue-green quetzal feathers, lay in the primordial sea and shaped the world by word and thought.

facets.facet_name: Feathered Serpent lord of Chichén Itzá
facets.core_claim: Kukulkan came with the Itzá, founded cities and ordered the land; his serpent body descends his temple to bless the people.

facets.facet_name: Heart of Sky, storm-creator and destroyer
facets.core_claim: Huracan is Heart of Sky who joined Gucumatz in the making of the world, and who sent the great flood and resin rain on the failed wooden people.

facets.facet_name: Sun-Faced Lord and jaguar of the night
facets.core_claim: K'inich Ajaw crosses the sky by day and the underworld by night as a jaguar; kings bear his name and his light.

facets.facet_name: Guide of those who die by the rope
facets.core_claim: Those who hang themselves go to the paradise beneath the great ceiba, and Ixtab comes for them.

facets.facet_name: The boastful false sun
facets.core_claim: Vucub Caquix proclaimed, "I am the sun, the light, the moon," but his brightness was a lie; the Twins shot him from his tree and stripped his glory.

facets.facet_name: Death lord of the earthquake and the punishing underworld
facets.core_claim: Kisin rules beneath the earth and torments the wicked dead; when he stirs, the earth quakes.

facets.facet_name: Grandmother who ground the maize into humanity
facets.core_claim: Xmucane ground the maize and mixed the water that became the flesh and blood of the first four men.

facets.facet_name: Uncreated creator without beginning or end
facets.core_claim: Coqui Xee was not made by anyone; all things and all gods come from him.

facets.facet_name: Lord of death and the underworld
facets.core_claim: Coqui Bezelao receives the dead in the underworld and is honored in the tombs of the ancestors.

facets.facet_name: Primordial creator couple
facets.core_claim: Before light, the god and goddess One Deer raised their stone palace above the waters; from them came the gods and the noble houses.

facets.facet_name: Plumed wind god who founded rule
facets.core_claim: Nine Wind came down from the heavens on a cord, set up the sky and the waters, and gave the Mixtec lords their insignia.

facets.facet_name: Rain god and patron of the People of the Rain
facets.core_claim: Dzahui sends the rain on which the Mixtec fields live; the people are his and bear his name.

facets.facet_name: Fire-sun patron of the Tarascan kings
facets.core_claim: Curicaueri is the great fire who leads the Uacúsecha; the king is his representative and must keep his fires fed with wood and conquest.

facets.facet_name: Moon goddess of crops
facets.core_claim: Xaratanga makes the fields fruitful and is a goddess of the people of the lake.

facets.facet_name: Creator mother who sends the rain
facets.core_claim: Cuerauáperi gives birth to the gods and raises the clouds from the east that water the land.

facets.facet_name: Thunderer with the sling who pours the rain
facets.core_claim: Illapa breaks his sister's water jar with his sling and the rain falls; his thunder and lightning are the voice and arm of heaven.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the sea and all waters
facets.core_claim: Mama Qucha is the ocean beneath the earth from which every spring and lake rises; she gives fish and calms the waves.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the maize
facets.core_claim: The finest ears are the Mama Sara; dressed and honored, they keep the maize strong and the harvest abundant.

facets.facet_name: Mountain lords and guardians
facets.core_claim: Each great peak is an Apu, a living lord who protects or punishes the people of its valleys according to their reciprocity.

facets.facet_name: Earth-Maker and oracle of the coast
facets.core_claim: Pachacamac animates the world; his oracle answers pilgrims from every province, and when he is angry the earth shakes.

facets.facet_name: Boneless creator who withheld the rain
facets.core_claim: Con made the world and its people, but in his anger turned the coast to desert; he was displaced by Pachacamac.

facets.facet_name: Fanged hero who fights the monsters
facets.core_claim: Ai Apaec wrestles the monsters of the sea and the earth and maintains the order that sacrifice sustains.

facets.facet_name: Snow-mountain god of rain and flood
facets.core_claim: Pariacaca came down as rain, hail and lightning and drove out Huallallo Carhuincho; the peoples of his slopes owe him worship.

facets.facet_name: The creator who walks as a beggar
facets.core_claim: Cuniraya Viracocha walked about like a poor man; with a word he raised terraces and canals, and those who mocked him learned too late who he was.

facets.facet_name: Bearded teacher of arts and law
facets.core_claim: Bochica walked among the Muisca teaching them to spin and weave, to farm and to live justly; he left his footprints in the rocks.

facets.facet_name: He who opened the falls to drain the flood
facets.core_claim: When the savanna was drowned, Bochica appeared on the rainbow and with a stroke of his golden staff split the rocks at Tequendama so the waters could pour away.

facets.facet_name: Rebel goddess of pleasure turned moon
facets.core_claim: Chía led people to feasting, dance and freedom against the teacher's law; for her flood she was sent to shine at night.

facets.facet_name: Punished god who bears the earth
facets.core_claim: Chibchacum sent the flood and was condemned by Bochica to carry the earth; when he moves it from one shoulder to the other, the ground trembles.

facets.facet_name: The sun of Sogamoso
facets.core_claim: Sué gives light and warmth to the savanna; his temple at Sogamoso held gold offered by the people.

facets.facet_name: Spirits of sickness and disorder
facets.core_claim: Wekufe bring illness and death; the machi climbs her rewe and battles them to restore the sick person's balance.

facets.facet_name: Serpent who raised the flood
facets.core_claim: Kai Kai Vilu made the waters rise and climb the hills to destroy humankind.

facets.facet_name: Serpent who raised the mountains to save the people
facets.core_claim: Treng Treng Vilu lifted the mountain above the flood; those who climbed him survived and became the ancestors.

facets.facet_name: The First Father who unfolded himself
facets.core_claim: Ñamandu, before the earth existed, unfolded his own divine body from the original darkness and created the foundation of the word.

facets.facet_name: Father of thunder and rain
facets.core_claim: Tupã dwells in the west and rides the storm; his thunder announces the rain that renews the earth.

facets.facet_name: Sun-twin culture hero
facets.core_claim: Kuaray, with his brother Jasy, defeated the jaguars who ate their mother and then rose to light the world.

facets.facet_name: Moon-twin
facets.core_claim: Jasy follows his brother through the sky; his mistakes and his darkened face come from the old adventures on earth.

facets.facet_name: Lawgiver of the sacred flutes
facets.core_claim: Yurupari gave men the flutes that are his voice and his body and the laws that govern marriage and initiation; whoever breaks his secrets dies.

facets.facet_name: Lady of the hurricane
facets.core_claim: When Guabancex is angry she raises the winds and the waters, overthrows houses and uproots trees.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Coaybay, house of the dead
facets.core_claim: Maquetaurie Guayaba rules Coaybay; the dead serve him there and come out at night in human form.

facets.facet_name: Dog guardian of the dead
facets.core_claim: Opiyelguobiran, the four-legged zemí, watches over the dead and would run into the woods at night until he was tied.

facets.facet_name: Hero who stole cassava and cohoba
facets.core_claim: Deminán and his brothers took cassava and the sacred snuff from the elder who guarded them; from the wound on his back came the mother of the people.

facets.facet_name: Sila, the breath and mind of the world
facets.core_claim: Sila is the air, the weather and the intelligence of the universe; it speaks not in words but in storm and calm, sunshine and the play of children, and the angakkuq listens.

facets.facet_name: Raven who made the land and brought light
facets.core_claim: Raven Father found himself in the dark, created the land and the animals, made the first man, and stole the daylight so people could see.

facets.facet_name: Chief of the shamans' helping spirits
facets.core_claim: Tornarsuk is the master of the tornait; the angakkuq who wins his help can travel to Sedna and to the moon and bring back healing and game.

facets.facet_name: Moon man who pursues his sister the sun
facets.core_claim: Aningaaq carries a torch that burns low as he chases Malina; he grows thin and vanishes for three days to eat, and returns.

facets.facet_name: Thunderbird who seizes whales
facets.core_claim: Thunderbird lives in the high mountains, carries off whales in his talons and wields the lightning snake; chiefs descended from him wear his crest.

facets.facet_name: Rock, the first being who emptied himself to create
facets.core_claim: Inyan was everywhere and all-powerful; to make another he opened his veins, and his blood became the waters and the sky, leaving him dry and hard.

facets.facet_name: Sky, judge of gods and humans
facets.core_claim: Skan is the energy that moves all things; he gives each being its spirit and holds council and judgment over the gods.

facets.facet_name: All Spirit who made the world on Turtle's back
facets.core_claim: Maheo made the waters, light and sky; with the coot's handful of mud he made the earth on the turtle's back, and from his own rib he made the first man and woman.

facets.facet_name: Prophet who brought the Sacred Arrows and the law
facets.core_claim: Sweet Medicine received the Sacred Arrows inside the holy mountain and gave the people their laws and council; he lived through four generations and warned of what would come.

facets.facet_name: Master of Breath, giver of life
facets.core_claim: Hesaketvmese holds the breath of all living things; at the Posketv the new fire is his gift of renewal.

facets.facet_name: Rabbit who stole fire
facets.core_claim: Rabbit danced at the sacred fire with resin in his hair, set it alight and ran, bringing fire to all the people.

facets.facet_name: Horned panther of the lake depths
facets.core_claim: Mishipeshu lashes his tail to raise the waves and drown those who cross without offering; the copper of Lake Superior is his.

facets.facet_name: Thunderbird grandfathers
facets.core_claim: The Animikiig fly in with the storm, shoot lightning at Mishipeshu and the serpents, and protect the people.

facets.facet_name: Transformer who shaped the land
facets.core_claim: Glooscap made the people from ash trees, tamed the animals, released the waters the monster held back, and paddled away promising to return.

facets.facet_name: Destructive wolf-twin
facets.core_claim: Malsumis was born the wrong way and wanted to kill his brother; he made what harms, and fell to Glooscap's fern-root.

facets.facet_name: Humpbacked flute player of fertility
facets.core_claim: Kokopelli plays and the snow melts and the crops come; he carries seeds and children on his back and courts young women.

facets.facet_name: God of germination
facets.core_claim: Muy'ingwa sits beneath the earth among the seeds; from him the corn and all plants come up.

facets.facet_name: The He-She All-Container
facets.core_claim: Before anything, only Awonawilona was; conceiving within, the All-Container became the sun and from it came all the generations of life.

facets.facet_name: Twin war gods and monster-slayers
facets.core_claim: The Ahayuuta brought the people up to the light and killed the monsters of the world; they are mischievous, fierce and forever guardians.

facets.facet_name: Horned serpent of the springs
facets.core_claim: Kolowisi guards the sacred springs; he brings water and life, and when angered he rises to flood the village.

facets.facet_name: She who creates by thinking
facets.core_claim: Thought Woman thinks and it is; she named the things of the world and taught the first sisters the way of life.

facets.facet_name: Corn Mother who receives the dead
facets.core_claim: Iyatiku gave the corn and the clans and returned to the place of emergence; the dead go home to her.

facets.facet_name: Spider Woman, teacher of weaving and helper of heroes
facets.core_claim: Spider Woman lives atop Spider Rock; she guided the Twins with her magic feathers and taught the Diné to weave the world into a blanket.

facets.facet_name: Holder of the creation bundle
facets.core_claim: First Man made the first hogan and set the world in order with his medicine bundle; from the same power came the knowledge of witchcraft.

facets.facet_name: First Woman, co-maker of the world
facets.core_claim: First Woman and First Man set out the world; in the quarrel of the sexes their wisdom and folly brought both order and the monsters.

facets.facet_name: Sun Bearer, father of the Twins
facets.core_claim: Jóhonaaʼéí carries the sun on his back; he tested his sons in sweat lodge and with spikes before giving them weapons of lightning.

facets.facet_name: First Angry, the trickster of disorder
facets.core_claim: Coyote scattered the stars that First Woman was placing carefully, stole Water Monster's child and caused the flood, and threw a stone in the water so that death would be permanent.

facets.facet_name: White Painted Woman, embodied in each girl's Sunrise Ceremony
facets.core_claim: In the Sunrise Ceremony the girl becomes White Painted Woman for four days, blessing the people with long life and her healing power.

facets.facet_name: Monster-slayer son of the rain
facets.core_claim: Child of Water, hidden from the giant under the fire pit, grew and killed the monsters with arrows his father gave him.

facets.facet_name: Elder monster-slaying brother
facets.core_claim: Killer of Enemies fought alongside Child of Water to rid the world of monsters.

facets.facet_name: Bringer of the Great Law of Peace
facets.core_claim: The Peacemaker brought the Good Mind; he buried the weapons beneath the Tree of Peace and gave the Confederacy its law, its council and its clan mothers.

facets.facet_name: Horned serpent of the crystal
facets.core_claim: The Uktena lurks in deep pools and high passes; its breath is poison, but the hero who kills it gains the ulunsuti, the crystal of seeing.

facets.facet_name: Twin sons who became the thunder
facets.core_claim: The two boys let the game out of the cave, found out Selu's secret, and after many adventures went to the west where they live as the Thunderers.

facets.facet_name: Coyote who readied the world for people
facets.core_claim: Coyote let himself be swallowed by the monster, cut its heart, and from its parts made the tribes; from its blood came the Nimiipuu.

facets.facet_name: Creator on the primal waters
facets.core_claim: Earth Initiate made the world from Turtle's mud and meant people to live without death or toil.

facets.facet_name: Coyote who brought death into the world
facets.core_claim: Coyote spoiled Earth Initiate's gift of deathlessness; when his son died first, he wept, but the rule could not be undone.

facets.facet_name: Admiral of the sea
facets.core_claim: Agwe rules the ocean in his ship Imamou; sailors and fishermen are his, and offerings are floated out to him on a raft (barque).

facets.facet_name: Simbi of the fresh waters and magic
facets.core_claim: Simbi lives in springs and streams, knows the leaves and the work of magic, and carries messages between the living and the dead.

facets.facet_name: Legba, linguist of Mawu-Lisa
facets.core_claim: Legba, youngest son of Mawu-Lisa, alone knows all the languages of the vodun; he carries messages and guards the gate of every compound and town.
